mainTopic: The water libation on סוכות, who mentions rain on שמיני עצרת, and why mentioning dew and wind is optional
overview: The גמרא continues discussing the water libation on סוכות, which is tied to when we start mentioning rain. It explains that רבי עקיבא takes the timing of the extra libation from the sixth day. It then brings רבי נתן, who learns from the wording 'הסך נסך' that there are two libations, one of water and one of wine. Next it asks who wrote the משנה that says the water is poured all seven days. A first answer, רבי יהודה בן בתירה together with רבי יהודה, is rejected. The final answer is that the משנה follows רבי יהושע, and the seven days are a הלכה למשה מסיני. The גמרא then asks which רבי יהושע and which בן בתירה said that on שמיני עצרת only the later prayer leader mentions rain. רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that both names refer to רבי יהושע בן בתירה. Finally, a ברייתא teaches that mentioning dew and wind is optional, because they are never held back, and the proof from אליהו continues on the next amud.

steps.title: If רבי עקיבא uses רבי יהודה בן בתירה's reading, why not follow him fully?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי עקיבא. If he accepts the reading of רבי יהודה בן בתירה, he should also start on the same day.
steps.simpleTranslation: If רבי עקיבא agrees with רבי יהודה בן בתירה, then he should rule like him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי עקיבא for borrowing only part of רבי יהודה בן בתירה's reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this, the גמרא explained that רבי עקיבא knows one of the two libations is water because of רבי יהודה בן בתירה's extra letters (מ, י, ם spelling מים). But רבי יהודה בן בתירה uses those letters to start from the second day of סוכות. So why does רבי עקיבא start only from the sixth day?

phrases.aramaic: אִי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָה —
phrases.english: If he holds like Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira,
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי עקיבא, who just used רבי יהודה בן בתירה's extra letters to prove one libation is water.

phrases.english: let him say like him!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָה — נֵימָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues from the earlier part of the daf, where רבי עקיבא's view was tied to רבי יהודה בן בתירה's reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's starting day (the sixth day)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If you accept someone's source, you should accept the result that comes from it, which here is starting from the second day.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא places the extra libation on the sixth day
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא holds that the word showing an extra libation appears on the sixth day, so that is where the water libation starts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא holds that the extra libation word is written about the sixth day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי עקיבא still starts on the sixth day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי עקיבא, the plural word ונסכיה ('its libations') on the sixth day is what actually shows there are two libations. רבי יהודה בן בתירה's letters only tell us the second libation is water, not when it begins. So the day comes from the sixth-day פסוק.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva holds:
when the extra libation is written,
phrases.notes: This is the plural word ונסכיה, 'its libations' (במדבר 29:31).

phrases.english: it is on the sixth day that it is written.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the source: one hint shows the extra libation is water, another hint shows the day.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Accepting רבי יהודה בן בתירה's letters would force starting from the second day.
steps.terutzMaskana: The letters only teach 'water'; the timing comes from the sixth-day word ונסכיה.

steps.title: רבי נתן learns two libations from 'הסך נסך'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי נתן learns from a פסוק with the libation word twice that there are two libations, one of water and one of wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי נתן says, 'In the holy place pour a libation of strong drink to ה׳.' The פסוק is talking about two libations, one of water and one of wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source, from רבי נתן, for the water libation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses two words for pouring, 'הסך' and 'נסך'. רבי נתן reads these as two separate libations. One is the regular wine, and the other is water.

keyTerms.meaning: Pour a libation (two forms of the same word)

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Natan says:
"In the holy place pour a libation of strong drink to the Lord"
the verse is speaking of two libations,
one is the water libation
and one is the wine libation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings another תנא's source for ניסוך המים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The double wording 'הסך נסך' points to two libations: water and wine.

steps.title: Maybe both libations are wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why both libations cannot be wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say that both of them are wine!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי נתן's reading. This sets up the next step, where it explains the wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two words for libation might mean two pourings, but nothing in the words says 'water'. So maybe both are wine.

phrases.english: Say both of them are of wine!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the derivation in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי נתן's claim that one libation is water
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Doubling the word shows two libations, not two different liquids.

steps.title: The different forms of the word show two different liquids
steps.stepSummary: If both were wine, the פסוק would use the same form twice. The change in form shows one is water and one is wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the פסוק should write either 'הסך הסך' or 'נסך נסך'. Why does it say 'הסך נסך'? Learn from this: one is water and one is wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by pointing to the exact wording of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two of the same thing would be written in the same form. Because the פסוק switches from ה to נ, it hints at two different kinds. So one libation is water and one is wine.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי נתן: the mixed wording 'הסך נסך' teaches two libations of two different liquids, water and wine.

phrases.english: If so, let the verse write
either "hasekh hesekh" or "nasekh nesekh";
what is "hasekh nesekh"?
phrases.notes: The first word starts with ה and the second with נ. That mismatch is the hint.

phrases.english: Learn from this:
one is of water and one is of wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of the פסוק's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two libation words could just mean two wine pourings.
steps.terutzMaskana: The change in the form of the word shows two different liquids.

steps.title: Who wrote the משנה that says water is poured all seven days?
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says water is poured all seven days, but none of the opinions so far gives seven days.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about the משנה that says the water libation is all seven days? Who wrote it? If רבי יהושע, it should be one day. If רבי עקיבא, two days. If רבי יהודה בן בתירה, six days!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges all the views by showing that none of them fits the משנה about seven days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each תנא gives a different number of days: רבי יהושע one, רבי עקיבא two (sixth and seventh), רבי יהודה בן בתירה six (second through seventh). None reaches seven. So whose opinion is that משנה?

keyTerms.meaning: That which we learned in a משנה

phrases.english: But that which we learned:
"The water libation is all seven days" — whose view is it?

phrases.aramaic: אִי רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ — נֵימָא חַד יוֹמָא,
phrases.english: If Rabbi Yehoshua, let it say one day;
if Rabbi Akiva, two days;

phrases.aramaic: אִי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָה — שִׁיתָּא יוֹמֵי!
phrases.english: if Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira, six days!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the different views on which days the water is poured.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה stating water libation all seven days
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: None of the known opinions produces seven days, so the משנה has no author.

steps.title: רבי יהודה בן בתירה, following רבי יהודה: drop the first day, add the eighth
steps.stepSummary: The משנה follows רבי יהודה בן בתירה, who agrees with רבי יהודה that water is poured on שמיני עצרת too. So he removes the first day and adds the eighth, making seven.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really it is רבי יהודה בן בתירה, and he holds like רבי יהודה in a משנה, who says the water was poured from a לוג all eight days. He takes out the first day and adds the eighth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the seven-day משנה is רבי יהודה בן בתירה, once you add in רבי יהודה's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה says water is poured on the eighth day, שמיני עצרת, as well. רבי יהודה בן בתירה does not pour on the first day, but he takes the eighth day from רבי יהודה. Second through eighth makes seven days.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually (really, it is as first said)
A measure of liquid; here, the vessel used for pouring

steps.whatToRemember: This answer says the seven-day משנה is רבי יהודה בן בתירה (start on day two) plus רבי יהודה (include day eight), giving days two to eight. Step 8 attacks this answer, and step 9 replaces it.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Seven days' here is not the first seven days of סוכות. It is the second day through שמיני עצרת.

phrases.aramaic: לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָה הִיא,
phrases.english: Actually, it is Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira,
and he holds like Rabbi Yehuda of the Mishnah.
As we learned: Rabbi Yehuda says:
With a log he would pour all eight days.
And he takes out the first and brings in the eighth.
phrases.notes: 'He' here is רבי יהודה בן בתירה. He keeps his own start on day two but adds day eight.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Combining two opinions to find the author of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה בן בתירה gives only six days, from the second through the seventh.
steps.terutzMaskana: Together with רבי יהודה's eighth day, he gives seven days, from the second through the eighth.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: This is only a first attempt. Step 8 shows it is inconsistent, and step 9 replaces it: the משנה follows רבי יהושע, and the seven days are a tradition.

steps.title: If day one is dropped, day eight should be dropped too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה בן בתירה drops the first day but adds the eighth. The hint for water ends on the seventh day, just as it begins on the second.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is special about the first day that no water is poured on it? Is it because the hint for water first shows up on the second day? Then the eighth day should be left out too, because the last hint for water shows up on the seventh day!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 7. It says רבי יהודה בן בתירה cannot use the hints in the פסוקים to cut out day one and still add day eight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה בן בתירה's water libation is built on hints in the פסוקים, starting from the second day. If the hints decide when the water starts, they should also decide when it ends. They stop at the seventh day, so there is no source for pouring on the eighth day. Being consistent would give only six days, not seven.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? It asks why two cases are treated differently.
Hinted at. The water is only hinted at in the פסוקים, not stated openly.
The eighth day, which is שמיני עצרת.

phrases.english: And what is different about the first day, that [water is] not [poured on it]?
Is it because when water is hinted at,
it is on the second day that it is hinted at?
phrases.notes: This points back to the extra letters in the פסוקים about the second day's offerings, where the first hint for water appears.

phrases.english: Then the eighth day too [should be left out],
because when water is hinted at,
it is on the seventh day that it is hinted at!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in Step 7, which credited the משנה to רבי יהודה בן בתירה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יהודה בן בתירה reaches seven days by dropping day one and adding day eight.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The hints in the פסוקים run from day two to day seven. If they set the starting point, they should also set the end point. Adding day eight is inconsistent.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי יהושע, who knows the seven days by tradition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the last answer. The משנה follows רבי יהושע, and the water libation on all seven days is a tradition, not something learned from the פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the משנה follows רבי יהושע. The water libation on all seven days was learned as a tradition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on tying the משנה to רבי יהודה בן בתירה. It gives a new answer: the seven days are a received tradition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every opinion so far tried to find the water libation in hints in the פסוקים, and none of them came out to exactly seven days. Here the hints are set aside. The seven days come from a tradition, so the count no longer has to match the hints.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals that the גמרא is dropping the earlier answer.
They learned it as a law by tradition, not from a פסוק.
The water libation, pouring water on the מזבח during סוכות.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבי יהושע with רבי יהודה בן בתירה or with רבי יהודה. The new answer is that the משנה follows רבי יהושע.

phrases.english: Rather: [the משנה] follows רבי יהושע,
and the water libation for all seven days,
they learned it as a law by tradition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge in Step 8 and replaces the earlier answer with a new one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the משנה to a different תנא and gives a different source for the law: a tradition instead of hints in the פסוקים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The seven days had to come from hints in the פסוקים, according to רבי יהודה בן בתירה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows רבי יהושע. The seven days of water libation are a tradition.

steps.title: Support: the water libation is a הלכה למשה מסיני
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחוניא lists three laws that are each a הלכה למשה מסיני: the ten saplings, the willow, and the water libation.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי אמי said that רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי נחוניא from the valley of בית חורתן: the ten saplings, the willow, and the water libation are each a law given to משה at סיני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its new answer. It shows that a known teaching already calls the water libation a tradition from סיני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in Step 9 said the water libation is a tradition. This teaching names the water libation outright as a הלכה למשה מסיני. That confirms that a law with no source in the פסוקים is still fully binding.

keyTerms.meaning: A law given to משה at סיני by word of mouth, without a written פסוק.
Ten saplings, a law about plowing before שמיטה.
The willow used around the מזבח on סוכות.

steps.whatToRemember: The water libation on all seven days of סוכות is a הלכה למשה מסיני. It does not depend on the hints in the פסוקים.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
phrases.english: As רבי אמי said that רבי יוחנן said

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי נְחוּנְיָא אִישׁ בִּקְעַת בֵּית חוֹרְתָן:
phrases.english: in the name of רבי נחוניא, a man of the valley of בית חורתן:
Ten saplings, the willow,
phrases.notes: Ten young trees spread over one field let you plow the whole field before שמיטה. The willow is the one used around the מזבח on סוכות.

phrases.english: and the water libation
are a law given to משה at סיני.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source that supports the claim in Step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That the water libation on all seven days is a tradition and not learned from a פסוק.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי נחוניא's teaching, passed on by רבי יוחנן and רבי אמי, that the water libation is a הלכה למשה מסיני.

steps.title: Which prayer leader mentions rain on שמיני עצרת and on פסח
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא goes on: רבי יהודה, quoting רבי יהושע, says that on שמיני עצרת the later prayer leader mentions rain and the earlier one does not. On the first day of פסח it is the other way around.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says in the name of רבי יהושע: on the last יום טוב of סוכות, the later prayer leader mentions rain and the earlier one does not. On the first יום טוב of פסח, the earlier prayer leader mentions rain and the later one does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to quoting the ברייתא. This part sets the exact point in the day when we start and stop mentioning rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are two prayer leaders on the same יום טוב, one earlier and one later. On שמיני עצרת the switch to mentioning rain happens with the later one. On the first day of פסח the switch away from mentioning rain also happens with the later one, so the earlier one still mentions it. The next part of the גמרא will need to explain this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who passes before the ark, meaning the חזן who leads the prayer.
Mentions, meaning he says the praise of rain, משיב הרוח ומוריד הגשם.
The last יום טוב of סוכות, which is שמיני עצרת.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: רבי יהודה says in the name of רבי יהושע:
The one who passes before the ark [to lead the prayer]
on the last יום טוב of the festival [of סוכות]:
the later one mentions [rain],
phrases.notes: The earlier leader leads שחרית and the later one leads מוסף.

phrases.english: the earlier one does not mention [rain].
On the first יום טוב of פסח:
the earlier one mentions [rain],
the later one does not mention [rain].

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of the water libation and goes back to the earlier ברייתא on the daf about when rain is mentioned (not רבי נתן's ברייתא of step 3).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On שמיני עצרת, mentioning rain begins with the later prayer leader. On the first day of פסח, the earlier prayer leader still mentions rain and the later one stops.

steps.title: Which רבי יהושע? Not the one in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which רבי יהושע is being quoted. It rejects the רבי יהושע of the משנה, because he says rain is mentioned on the last festival day itself, which sounds like from the very start of the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which רבי יהושע is this? If you say it is the רבי יהושע of our משנה, that cannot be, because he said that rain is mentioned on the last festival day of סוכות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which רבי יהושע said that only the later prayer leader mentions rain. It tries the רבי יהושע of the משנה, and that does not fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהושע says rain is mentioned 'on the last festival day', which means the whole day, starting from the night prayer. But the ברייתא in step 11 says the earlier prayer leader does NOT mention rain. So these two cannot be the same opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (offering a possible answer to test it)
Mentions (here, mentions rain in the prayer)

steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions agree that rain is mentioned on שמיני עצרת. The only question is WHEN on that day it starts: from the first prayer, or only from the later one.

phrases.english: Which Rabbi Yehoshua?
phrases.notes: He means the רבי יהושע quoted in the ברייתא from step 11.

phrases.english: If you say it is the Rabbi Yehoshua of our Mishnah,
but he said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּיוֹם טוֹב הָאַחֲרוֹן שֶׁל חַג הוּא מַזְכִּיר.
phrases.english: On the last festival day of the Festival, one mentions rain.
phrases.notes: Saying 'on the day' sounds like the whole day, from the night prayer on. So even the first prayer leader would mention it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions who the רבי יהושע is in the ruling quoted in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: Saying that the רבי יהושע of step 11 is the רבי יהושע of the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's רבי יהושע has rain mentioned for the whole last festival day, which clashes with the ruling that the earlier prayer leader does not mention it.

steps.title: Not the רבי יהושע of the ברייתא either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries the רבי יהושע of the ברייתא. He also does not fit, because he says rain is mentioned from the moment the לולב is put down, which is right at the start of שמיני עצרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is the רבי יהושע of the ברייתא. But he said rain is mentioned from the time the לולב is put down!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second option, the רבי יהושע of the ברייתא, and shows that he does not fit either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The לולב is put down when the seventh day of סוכות ends. So by his opinion, rain is already mentioned at the very first prayer of שמיני עצרת. That again clashes with the ruling that the earlier prayer leader does not mention it.

keyTerms.meaning: Of the ברייתא (a teaching from the time of the משנה that was not put into the משנה)

phrases.english: Rather, it is the Rabbi Yehoshua of the Baraita,
but didn't he say: from the time one puts it down?
phrases.notes: 'It' is the לולב, which is put down when the seventh day ends. So rain is mentioned from the start of שמיני עצרת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first option fails, tries a second option and rejects it too.
steps.kashyaTarget: Saying that the רבי יהושע of step 11 is the רבי יהושע of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He starts mentioning rain once the לולב is put down, which means at the first prayer of שמיני עצרת. That does not match 'the earlier prayer leader does not mention it.'

steps.title: A second ברייתא: which בן בתירה?
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא gives the same ruling in the name of 'בן בתירה'. The גמרא asks which בן בתירה this is. It cannot be רבי יהודה בן בתירה, because he starts mentioning rain on the second day of סוכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, there is a ברייתא where רבי יהודה says in the name of בן בתירה: on the last festival day of סוכות, the later prayer leader mentions rain. Which בן בתירה? If you say רבי יהודה בן בתירה, he said rain is mentioned starting on the second day of the festival!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a second, similar problem. A different ברייתא gives the same ruling in the name of 'בן בתירה', and the obvious בן בתירה does not fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה בן בתירה holds that rain is mentioned from the second day of סוכות, as the גמרא quoted from him earlier on the daf. So for him, rain is surely mentioned by everyone on שמיני עצרת. He cannot be the one who says only the later prayer leader mentions it.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who passes before the ark (the prayer leader)
Son of בתירה (a name that could fit more than one person)

phrases.english: And furthermore, that which was taught in a Baraita:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם בֶּן בְּתִירָה:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says in the name of ben Beteira:
The one who passes before the ark
on the last festival day of the Festival —
the later one mentions rain.
Which ben Beteira?
If you say Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira —

phrases.aramaic: הָא אָמַר: בַּשֵּׁנִי בֶּחָג הוּא מַזְכִּיר!
phrases.english: but he said: one mentions rain on the second day of the Festival!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, parallel problem of identity next to the one in steps 12 and 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: Saying that the 'בן בתירה' in the second ברייתא is רבי יהודה בן בתירה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה בן בתירה starts mentioning rain on the second day of סוכות, so he would never hold back the first prayer leader on שמיני עצרת.

steps.title: Both refer to רבי יהושע בן בתירה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that both ברייתות mean רבי יהושע בן בתירה. Sometimes he was called by his own name (רבי יהושע) and sometimes by his father's name (בן בתירה). One way was used before he got סמיכה, and the other after.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: say it is רבי יהושע בן בתירה. Sometimes he is called by his own name, and sometimes by his father's name. This one was from before he got סמיכה, and this one was from after.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק solves both problems with one answer. The 'רבי יהושע' and the 'בן בתירה' are the same person, a third sage who holds this exact ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both earlier problems came from guessing the wrong sage. Once we know there is a רבי יהושע בן בתירה, both ברייתות fit him. The different names just reflect his status: before סמיכה he was called by his father's name, and after סמיכה he was called 'רבי יהושע'.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it be (let us say it is)
That they ordained him (gave him סמיכה)

steps.whatToRemember: The ruling that only the later prayer leader on שמיני עצרת mentions rain belongs to רבי יהושע בן בתירה. He appears as 'רבי יהושע' in one ברייתא and as 'בן בתירה' in the other.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Let it be Rabbi Yehoshua ben Beteira,
sometimes he calls him by his own name,
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי יהודה, who quotes him in both ברייתות.

phrases.english: and sometimes he calls him by his father's name.
And this one was before they ordained him,
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא that calls him just 'בן בתירה', since he did not yet have the title 'רבי'.

phrases.english: and this one was after they ordained him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: תְּהֵא בְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן בְּתִירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problems of identity raised in steps 12, 13 and 14 all at once.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying a different speaker: both names point to one sage, רבי יהושע בן בתירה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought 'רבי יהושע' meant the well-known רבי יהושע, and 'בן בתירה' meant רבי יהודה בן בתירה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both mean רבי יהושע בן בתירה, who was named differently before and after his סמיכה, and he holds that only the later prayer leader on שמיני עצרת mentions rain.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a name in a ברייתא can point to a less famous sage, and that one person can be called by different names at different stages of his life.

steps.title: Mentioning dew and wind is optional
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the חכמים did not require mentioning dew (טל) and wind (רוחות) in the תפילה, but a person may mention them if he wants.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: the חכמים did not require anyone to mention dew and winds in the תפילה. But if someone wants to mention them, he may.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about dew and wind. Until now the topic was mentioning rain. Now we hear that dew and wind work differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Mentioning rain (גשמים) is required in its season. Dew and wind are different: there is no requirement, but there is also nothing wrong with mentioning them. This sets up the question in the next step: why is there a difference?

keyTerms.meaning: To mention (in the second ברכה of שמונה עשרה)

phrases.english: It was taught: regarding dew and winds,
the Sages did not require one to mention them.
phrases.notes: "Mention" here means adding them into the second ברכה of שמונה עשרה, the same way we mention rain.

phrases.english: But if one wants to mention them, he may mention them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the discussion of when rain is mentioned to a related rule about dew and wind.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mentioning dew and wind in the תפילה is optional: not required, but allowed.

steps.title: Why is it optional?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why mentioning dew and wind is optional, unlike rain.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the ברייתא's rule. This is a setup line: the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rain must be mentioned, so why not dew and wind? The גמרא wants to know what makes them different.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ruling in step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why mentioning dew and wind is optional while mentioning rain is required.

steps.title: Dew and wind are never held back
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא answers that dew and wind are never held back, so there is no need to ask for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: because they are never held back.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא gives the reason: dew and wind always come.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rain can be held back as a punishment, so we must mention it and recognize that it comes from השם. Dew and wind always come, so mentioning them is not required, though it is still allowed.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said:
Because they are not held back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Dew and wind are never held back, so mentioning them is not required.

steps.title: Where do we learn that dew is never held back?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source that dew is never held back.
steps.simpleTranslation: And dew, where do we learn that it is not held back?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wants a source for רבי חנינא's claim about dew. This sets up the proof from a פסוק that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא said dew is never held back. The גמרא asks how we know this, and starts with dew specifically.

phrases.english: And dew, from where do we know that it is not held back

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a source for the reason given in step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that dew is never held back.

steps.title: Proof from אליהו and אחאב
steps.stepSummary: אליהו swore there would be no dew or rain. Later השם told him He would send rain, but did not mention dew. The גמרא starts to explain why.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: "And אליהו התשבי, of the settlers of גלעד, said to אחאב: As השם the God of Israel lives, before Whom I stand, there will be no dew or rain these years except by my word." And it is written: "Go, show yourself to אחאב, and I will send rain upon the land." But dew He did not mention to him. What is the reason? Because...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two פסוקים. אליהו stopped both dew and rain, but when השם ended the drought He only promised rain, not dew. The גמרא begins asking why, and the answer continues in the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If dew had really been stopped, השם would have had to promise to bring it back too. Since only rain is promised, it seems dew never actually stopped. The reason is finished in the next part of the גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: אחאב, the wicked king of Israel

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is saying אליהו's oath failed. The point is only that השם did not need to promise dew. The full explanation comes right after.

phrases.english: As it is written: "And Elijah the Tishbite said,
who was of the settlers of Gilead, to Ahab:
As the Lord, God of Israel, lives,
before Whom I stand,

phrases.aramaic: אִם יִהְיֶה הַשָּׁנִים הָאֵלֶּה טַל וּמָטָר
phrases.english: there will be no dew or rain in these years
except by my word."
And it is written: "Go, show yourself to Ahab,
and I will send rain upon the land."
But dew He did not say to him.
What is the reason? Because...

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source requested in step 19.
steps.raayaObject: That dew is never held back.
steps.raayaSupportSource: מלכים א 17:1 and 18:1: dew and rain were both included in אליהו's oath, but only rain is promised when the drought ends.
